description: Fixed-part operators ':', '*', '/', '^' and '-', the order of terms and of their variables, and the choice between contrasts and indicators in each term.

cases.description: '*' crosses two factors: both main effects use contrasts, as does the interaction.
The expanded form gives the same IR as interactions-01.
An interaction without its main effects codes both factors by indicators, as R does.
With 'a' in the formula, 'b' in 'a:b' uses contrasts, since 'a' is an earlier term, and 'a' uses indicators, since 'b' is not.
A numeric variable crossed with a factor.
A numeric-by-factor interaction without the factor's margin codes the factor by indicators.
Without an intercept, the first categorical variable of the first term that has one is coded by indicators, and the later factors by contrasts.
Without an intercept, 'b' sorts before 'x:a' and takes the indicators. In 'x:a', 'a' uses contrasts, since 'x' is an earlier term.
Without an intercept, the first categorical variable met, 'b' in 'z:b', already uses indicators, so 'a' in 'z:b:a' keeps its contrasts.
'^' gives every product of the terms up to the power.
'^' is the interaction of the terms with themselves, so the order within a degree follows that product: 'x:z' comes before 'a:b'.
'/' nests: 'a/b' is 'a + a:b'.
'/' with a sum on the left nests within all its variables together.
'-' removes a term that is present.
'+' and '-' apply from left to right, so the term added again comes last.
The variables of a term follow their first appearance in the fixed part, so 'b:a' keeps 'b' first and 'b' varies fastest.
':' distributes over sums.
A variable crossed with itself is the variable.
A three-way factorial, with terms sorted by degree.
In 'x:b', 'b' uses contrasts because 'x' lies within the earlier term 'a:x'.
Sum coding on both factors of an interaction.
Mean centring applies wherever the variable appears, including the interaction.
An empty cell of 'a:b' leaves a column of zeros, which the sequential rule drops.
'w' equals 'x' plus 'z', and the sequential rule drops the later member of the dependency, 'w'.
The data of interactions-24 with 'w' written first: the sequential rule now drops 'z'.
Near the tolerance 1e-7: 'u' has a relative residual of about 1e-6 and is kept, and 'v' one of about 1e-9 and is dropped.
